Prenatal Genetic Diagnosis Testing for the HBB gene by Sanger Sequencing

Indications

The genetic reports of Mrs. Rinki Devi and Mr. Jitender Kumar were suggestive of Beta-thalassemia trait and were found to be carriers of c.-138C>T variant in the HBB gene. The AF of Mrs. Rinki Devi was referred for the genetic evaluation of the HBB gene.

Sample:
Amniotic Fluid (AF)
Sample Quality:
Optimal
Maternal Cell Contamination (MCC) status
No maternal cell contamination was detected and the report for same has been released on 5th September, 2024

Result

Mutation Nomenclature Result
HBB (NM_000518.5) : c.-138C>T
 DETECTED (HETEROZYGOUS)

Interpretation

Sanger testing of AF of Mrs. Rinki Devi detected the HBB (NM_000518.5), c.-138C>T variant in the heterozygous state. This suggests that the fetus of Mrs. Rinki Devi is likely to be a carrier of the HBB variant detected in the parents.
 
Recommendation
  • Genetic counseling is recommended.
  • Parental testing is highly recommended to confirm the HBB gene variants. 
Test Information
  1. Sanger testing and analysis was performed only for the exons and exon-intron boundaries in the HBB gene.
  2. This test is designed to detect mutations in the above-mentioned regions only. Sequences surrounding the regions of interest are analyzed but not reported. 
  3. Extremely rare de novo variants, certain promoter and rare intronic mutations may not be assessed. 
  4. This assay does not detect any deletion or duplication except that mentioned in the test description.  
  5. Unless reported or predicted to cause disease, alterations found that do not result in an amino acid substitution are  not  reported. These alterations and common polymorphisms identified for this patient will be available upon request.

Methodology

  1. Bi-directional DNA sequencing was carried out using 3500/3730XL Genetic Analyzer Applied Biosystems (ABI) for all exons (coding regions) and exon–intron boundaries to detect uncommon point mutations and small rearrangements in the HBB gene. 
  2. The 619 bp deletion was carried out by end point PCR (gel electrophoresis). 
  3. The data was analyzed using CodonCode Aligner v5.0.2 (CodonCode Corporation, Centerville, MA, USA) and/or Mutation Surveyor v5.0 (Softgenetics, State College, PA, USA).
Limitations
  1. Although all precautions are taken during Molecular Genetic testing the currently available data indicate that the technical error rate for all types of DNA analysis is approximately 2%. 
  2. In rare cases because of allele  dropout/large deletions on one allele, heterozygosity may be reported as homozygosity. 
  3. Results have been confirmed by bidirectional sequencing, with the error rate of the Taq polymerase for base incorporation being 1 in 6000 bases. 
  4. This assay is unable to differentiate between cis and trans mutations.
  5.  Please note that Chorionic Villus Samples (CVS) or Amniotic Fluid (AF) may possibly be contaminated by maternal blood and this may rarely cause false negative or false positive results in spite of utilization of standard assays (STR) to rule out maternal cell contamination (MCC). This should be noted before making any clinical decision and the patient should be counseled accordingly by the clinician. 
  6. For test performed on specimens received or collected from non-NCGM locations, it is presumed that the specimen belongs to the patient named or identified as labeled on the container/test request and such verification has been carried out at the point of generation of the said specimen by the sender.
  7. This test has not been approved by external accrediting bodies and has been validated according to internal laboratory criteria. Accreditation is not required for the reporting of these test results. 
  8. The test has been performed by the laboratory with the assumption that counseling regarding its utility as well as limitations has been conveyed by the referring clinician to the patient/ guardian/family and consent for the same has been obtained after relevant pre-test counseling.
Disclaimer: Sex of the fetus is not disclosed in accordance with the Indian PC & PNDT Act 1994.
